requirements.title: Delimiter tokens have seven listed spellings
requirements.source: 6.2.6 p1; J3/24-007 PDF page 70, printed page 56, line 29.
requirements.definition: When a lexical token serves as a delimiter, its spelling comes from (, ), /, [, ], (/, and /). The last two are the exact two-character delimiter spellings (/ and /). This classification presupposes a delimiter token; it does not make every occurrence of one of these characters a delimiter. The enclosing grammar decides the permitted context, pairing, and contents.
requirements.oracle: Four separately compiled positive controls cover the seven spellings in legal contexts. The parenthesis pair groups (left + right) before multiplication and checks 20 for left=2 and right=3. Two single slash delimiters enclose an integer DATA value list whose two separately checked results are 11 and 17. A square-bracket constructor supplies the two values 5 and 9 to an explicitly shaped integer array. A separate (/ ... /) constructor supplies 6 and 10. Each array element is checked independently; all values and shapes are defined before use, and every program terminates without a loop.
requirements.oracle_limitation: These are admission controls, not full construct semantics or direct observations of internal token boundaries. No malformed-pair or arbitrary-character rejection is inferred from the list. In particular, / used for division, the operators // and /=, and punctuation inside character constants or comments are not automatically delimiter tokens. Equals, =>, comma, colon, ::, semicolon, .., ?, and % are separate 6.2.1 alternatives rather than additional members of this seven-item list. Parenthesis pairs and each array-constructor pair occur together in their conforming controls; this is not independent proof of opening/closing-token diagnostics. Detailed DATA, expression, constructor, coarray, FORMAT, blank, and continuation rules remain with their defining sections. A diagnostic claim would require the applicable enclosing syntax/constraint or Clause 6 source-form/character obligation under 4.2, so none is manufactured here.
requirements.dependencies: 6.2.1 supplies the lexical-token union. R1001 and 10.1.3 admit and interpret the parenthesized integer expression (PDF 168, 172-173). 8.6.7 R840-R842/R848 and p8/p10 give the slash-delimited DATA context and one-to-one initialization of two same-type scalar integers (PDF 136-138). 7.8 R777-R781/C7120 and p1/p2/p6 admit both constructor spellings and specify the ordered rank-one values (PDF 114-115); R779 and R780 retain canonical ownership of bracket syntax. 10.2.1.3 supplies assignment to the same-shape integer arrays. 6.3.2.2-6.3.2.5 and 7.4.4.3 retain source-form and character-context rules; 6.2.4 and Clause 10 retain operator syntax. 4.2 p2(1) supplies conforming execution, while p2(3)/(5) concerns actual numbered-syntax/constraint or source-form/character violations.

accounting.rationale: PDF 70, printed 56, line 29: account separately for the delimiter-token premise and all seven enumerated spellings. No further paragraph, numbered rule, note, or table belongs to this section.

The sentence applies to a lexical token that is a delimiter. Character/comment contents and operators are not reclassified merely because they contain one of the same characters; ordinary valid programs do not expose scanner tokenization.
Spelling (: admitted with its matching right parenthesis around an R1001 expression.
Spelling ): admitted with its matching left parenthesis around an R1001 expression.
Spelling /: use R841 DATA delimiters, not the same character's division-operator role.
Spelling [: R777/R779 supplies a legal array-constructor opening without transferring the canonical numbered rule.
Spelling ]: R777/R780 supplies the matching array-constructor closing.
Preserve the two-character spelling (/ exactly in the first R777 constructor alternative.
Preserve the two-character spelling /) exactly in the first R777 constructor alternative.

review_rationale: Coordinator review independent of the draft authors; see doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_003.json. The delimiter-token premise and all seven spellings, including the two-character constructor delimiters, are accounted for. Matched pairs are positive controls in legal expression, DATA, and array-constructor contexts, not scanner-token-count or arbitrary-character rejection evidence.
